justification: Assessment reported INVALID and localized the first fatal step to lines 0061-0063, the sentence 'In either case, S has no neighbor in W_m, since S ⊇ R_{m-1}'. That is exactly the ground-truth flaw: the padded set S = R_{m-1} ∪ (arbitrary W_{m-1} vertices) in case |R_{m-1}| < n/2 is not known to avoid neighbors in W_m, since enlarging a set enlarges its neighborhood (N(S) ⊇ N(R_{m-1}) gives no upper bound), so N(S) ⊆ V\W_m and |N(S)| ≤ αn do not follow. The assessment states the same unsoundness in the same case, notes the padding vertices are merely unreachable from W_1 with no restriction on adjacency to W_m, and even supplies the standard repair (induct on |R_i| ≥ n/2). No explicit numeric counterexample was given, but the ground truth's witness (n=6, W_1={0,1}, W_2={2,3,4}, W_3={5}, S={2,3,4}, N(S)∩W_3={5}) instantiates precisely the inference the assessment rejects. Same defect.
